title: John Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 9.

questions.question: In John 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The man washed in the pool of Siloam
The Pharisees were brought a man
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus saw a blind man
questions.explanation: This event occurs first in the chapter as stated in John 9:1.

questions.question: Who did the disciples ask about the blind man?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: The disciples asked Jesus about the blind man as stated in John 9:2.

questions.question: What was Jesus' response regarding the sin of the blind man or his parents?
questions.correctAnswer: Neither hath this man sinned
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that neither the man nor his parents had sinned in John 9:3.

questions.question: What did Jesus say he must do while it is day?
options: Work the works of him that sent me
questions.correctAnswer: Work the works of him that sent me
questions.explanation: Jesus mentioned this in John 9:4.

questions.question: What did Jesus claim to be while he was in the world?
questions.correctAnswer: The light of the world
questions.explanation: Jesus declared this in John 9:5.

questions.question: What did Jesus use to anoint the eyes of the blind man?
questions.correctAnswer: Clay made of spittle
questions.explanation: Jesus made clay of the spittle and anointed the man's eyes as stated in John 9:6.

questions.question: Where did Jesus tell the blind man to wash?
questions.correctAnswer: In the pool of Siloam
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed the blind man to wash in the pool of Siloam in John 9:7.

questions.question: What did the neighbours question about the man who was blind?
options: Is he the one who sat and begged?
questions.correctAnswer: Is he the one who sat and begged?
questions.explanation: The neighbours questioned if he was the one who sat and begged as stated in John 9:8.

questions.question: What did some people say about the blind man when they saw him after he was healed?
questions.correctAnswer: He is like him
questions.explanation: Some said he is like the blind man, as mentioned in John 9:9.

questions.question: How did the blind man respond when asked how his eyes were opened?
options: A man called Jesus made clay
I was healed by the Pharisees
questions.correctAnswer: A man called Jesus made clay
questions.explanation: The blind man explained that Jesus made clay and anointed his eyes in John 9:11.

questions.question: What day was it when Jesus made the clay and opened the blind man's eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: The Sabbath day
questions.explanation: It was the Sabbath day when these events occurred, as noted in John 9:14.

questions.question: True or False: The blind man was born blind.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that the man was blind from his birth in John 9:1.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that the blind man's parents were the cause of his blindness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jesus clarified that neither the blind man nor his parents sinned, indicating they were not the cause of his blindness as stated in John 9:3.

questions.question: True or False: The blind man knew where Jesus was after he was healed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The blind man stated, 'I know not' when asked where Jesus was in John 9:12.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples believed the blind man had sinned.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The disciples asked Jesus who had sinned, indicating they were unsure, but Jesus clarified that neither had sinned in John 9:2-3.

medium.title: John Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the man who was healed say about how he received his sight?
options: He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see.
Jesus laid hands on my eyes, and I opened them.
I prayed and suddenly I could see.
A prophet touched my eyes and I was healed.
questions.correctAnswer: He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see.
questions.explanation: John 9:15 records the man saying, 'He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see.'

questions.question: What does John 9:22 promise will happen if someone confesses that Jesus is Christ as stated in John 9:21?
options: They will be put out of the synagogue.
They will be praised by the Pharisees.
They will be given a place of honor.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be put out of the synagogue.
questions.explanation: John 9:22 explains that the Jews had agreed that if anyone confessed Jesus as Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue, which connects to the man being of age to speak for himself in John 9:21.

questions.question: How did the healed man respond when asked what Jesus had done to open his eyes?
options: I have told you already, and ye did not hear.
Jesus prayed over me and I was healed.
He anointed my eyes and I received sight.
I do not know who healed me.
questions.correctAnswer: I have told you already, and ye did not hear.
questions.explanation: John 9:27 states, 'I have told you already, and ye did not hear,' showing his frustration with their repeated questioning.

questions.question: How did the parents' fear of the Jews influence their response about their son's healing?
options: They deflected the question to their son to avoid trouble.
They openly declared Jesus as the healer.
They refused to answer any questions.
They claimed the healing was a miracle from God.
questions.correctAnswer: They deflected the question to their son to avoid trouble.
questions.explanation: John 9:22 explains the parents feared the Jews because of the threat of being put out of the synagogue if they confessed Christ, so they told the questioners to ask their son (John 9:21, 23).

questions.question: What does the division among the Pharisees in John 9:16 teach about faith and judgment?
options: People often judge miracles based on their own biases and beliefs.
Miracles are always unanimously accepted by religious leaders.
Faith requires seeing and touching before believing.
Judgment should be quick and without question.
questions.correctAnswer: People often judge miracles based on their own biases and beliefs.
questions.explanation: John 9:16 shows Pharisees divided; some reject Jesus because He broke Sabbath, others marvel at the miracle despite considering Him a sinner, revealing biased judgment.

questions.question: How can the healed blind man’s response to being called a disciple challenge Christians today?
options: It encourages standing firm in faith despite opposition.
It teaches to avoid identifying with controversial figures.
It suggests always agreeing with religious authorities.
It advises keeping faith a private matter.
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages standing firm in faith despite opposition.
questions.explanation: In John 9:28, the man is accused of being Jesus’ disciple and reviled, yet he does not deny it, modeling courage in confessing faith.

questions.question: What practical lesson about honesty can be learned from the healed man's statement in John 9:25?
options: He honestly acknowledges what he knows without speculation.
He avoids answering questions to please others.
He changes his story to gain favor.
He refuses to speak about the healing.
questions.correctAnswer: He honestly acknowledges what he knows without speculation.
questions.explanation: John 9:25 shows integrity as he says, 'Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.'

questions.question: What does the healed man’s willingness to speak for himself in John 9:21-23 teach about personal responsibility in faith?
options: Mature believers should take responsibility for their own testimony.
Parents are always responsible for their children's faith.
Faith should be kept silent to avoid persecution.
Others should always speak for us in matters of faith.
questions.correctAnswer: Mature believers should take responsibility for their own testimony.
questions.explanation: John 9:21, 23 show the parents deferring to their son, encouraging him to speak for himself, highlighting personal accountability in faith.

questions.question: What does the man’s statement in John 9:17 reveal about recognizing Jesus’ identity through works?
options: He recognizes Jesus as a prophet based on the miracle.
He claims Jesus is just an ordinary man.
He denies Jesus’ involvement in his healing.
He calls Jesus a sinner for breaking the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: He recognizes Jesus as a prophet based on the miracle.
questions.explanation: John 9:17 says, 'He is a prophet,' showing the man’s faith in Jesus’ divine authority demonstrated through healing.

questions.question: How does John 9:24-25 illustrate the tension between human judgment and personal experience?
options: The man trusts his own experience over the Pharisees’ accusations.
The Pharisees accept the man’s testimony without question.
The man refuses to answer the Pharisees.
The Pharisees praise the miracle openly.
questions.correctAnswer: The man trusts his own experience over the Pharisees’ accusations.
questions.explanation: In John 9:24-25, despite being called a sinner, the man insists on his personal experience of healing as truth.

questions.question: Why did the Pharisees question the parents instead of accepting the blind man's testimony immediately, according to John 9:18-19?
options: They doubted the man had been born blind and wanted confirmation.
They wanted to honor the parents for their faith.
They were curious about the family’s background.
They believed the parents caused the blindness.
questions.correctAnswer: They doubted the man had been born blind and wanted confirmation.
questions.explanation: John 9:18-19 shows the Jews did not believe the man’s story and questioned his parents to verify his blindness and healing.

questions.question: What does John 9:16 teach about the challenge of recognizing God’s work when it conflicts with human traditions?
options: Some reject God’s work because it breaks their traditions.
God’s work always conforms to human rules.
Miracles are only accepted on the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: Some reject God’s work because it breaks their traditions.
questions.explanation: John 9:16 shows some Pharisees rejected Jesus because He healed on the Sabbath, revealing tension between God’s work and human traditions.

questions.question: How do the parents’ answers in John 9:20-21 demonstrate a balance between honesty and fear?
options: They confirm the facts but avoid attributing the miracle to Jesus.
They deny their son was ever blind.
They refuse to answer any questions.
questions.correctAnswer: They confirm the facts but avoid attributing the miracle to Jesus.
questions.explanation: John 9:20-21 shows the parents honestly confirm their son’s blindness and healing but do not explain how it happened due to fear (John 9:22).

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees agreed unanimously that the man healed by Jesus was not of God because he broke the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 9:16 states there was division among the Pharisees; some said he was not of God for breaking Sabbath, others questioned how a sinner could do miracles.

questions.question: True or False: The healed man’s parents were completely open and unafraid to speak about Jesus before the Pharisees.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: John 9:22 explains the parents feared the Jews because they had agreed to expel anyone confessing Christ, so they avoided attributing the miracle to Jesus.

hard.title: John Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 9.

questions.question: What did the blind man say when asked how his eyes were opened?
options: A man that is called Jesus made clay
questions.correctAnswer: A man that is called Jesus made clay
questions.explanation: In John 9:11, the blind man explained that Jesus made clay and anointed his eyes, which is how he received sight.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the Pharisees to the blind man's healing?
questions.correctAnswer: They cast him out
questions.explanation: In John 9:34, the Pharisees cast the healed man out after he asserted that Jesus must be of God.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask the blind man after he was cast out?
options: Do you believe on the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Do you believe on the Son of God?
questions.explanation: In John 9:35, Jesus sought the blind man and asked him if he believed in the Son of God.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean by saying 'For judgment I am come into this world'?
questions.correctAnswer: To bring light
questions.explanation: In John 9:39, Jesus indicates that his coming is to provide spiritual insight, highlighting the contrast between spiritual blindness and sight.

questions.question: What did the blind man respond when Jesus asked if he believed in the Son of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Who is he, Lord?
questions.explanation: In John 9:36, the blind man sought to know the identity of the Son of God to believe in him.

questions.question: What did the man say about Jesus after his healing?
questions.correctAnswer: He is a prophet
questions.explanation: In John 9:17, the blind man stated that Jesus, who healed him, is a prophet.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ὁράω' (horaō) in John 9:11 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To see
questions.explanation: 'ὁράω' (horaō) means 'to see' in Greek, which is fundamental to the narrative of the blind man's healing.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Jesus' statement about judgment in John 9:39?
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The irony lies in Jesus bringing sight to the blind while condemning those who claim to see yet remain spiritually blind, as seen in John 9:39.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of spiritual blindness in John 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 15:14
questions.explanation: Matthew 15:14 echoes the theme of spiritual blindness, as Jesus refers to the Pharisees as blind leaders of the blind, similar to the situation in John 9.

questions.question: What does the blind man declare about his previous condition in John 9:25?
options: I was blind, now I see
questions.correctAnswer: I was blind, now I see
questions.explanation: In John 9:25, the blind man succinctly summarizes his miraculous transformation by stating he was blind and now can see.

questions.question: What is said about Jesus regarding the Sabbath in John 9:16?
questions.correctAnswer: He breaks it
questions.explanation: In John 9:16, some Pharisees claim that Jesus is not from God because he does not keep the Sabbath, indicating he broke the customary laws.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jesus' statement about the judgment in John 9:39?
questions.correctAnswer: The man worshipped him
questions.explanation: John 9:38 shows that the man worshipped Jesus right before Jesus spoke about judgment, setting the context for his statement.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'God heareth not sinners' in John 9:31?
options: It highlights the power of prayer
It indicates Jesus was a sinner
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes God's justice
questions.explanation: In John 9:31, the statement emphasizes God's justice by asserting that God does not listen to those who are unrepentant sinners, highlighting the character of true worship.

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees acknowledged Jesus as a prophet.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Pharisees dismissed Jesus as a sinner and did not recognize him as a prophet, as seen in John 9:16 and 9:34.

questions.question: True or False: The blind man's parents feared the Jews and did not speak freely about Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In John 9:22, it is stated that the parents feared the Jews, which influenced their cautious responses regarding Jesus.

theological.title: John Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 9:3 teach about the origin of suffering and divine purpose?
options: Suffering is always a direct result of personal sin
God uses suffering to manifest His works and glory
Parents are responsible for their children's suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God uses suffering to manifest His works and glory
questions.explanation: John 9:3 explicitly states that neither the man nor his parents sinned, but that the works of God should be made manifest in him, indicating God's sovereign purpose in allowing suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' self-identification and mission is taught in John 9:5?
options: Jesus claims to be the Son of David
Jesus identifies as the light of the world during His earthly ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus identifies as the light of the world during His earthly ministry
questions.explanation: John 9:5 shows Jesus declaring Himself 'the light of the world' while He is present in the world, highlighting His role in bringing spiritual illumination.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the nature of divine healing and signs does John 9:33 teach?
options: Miracles can be done through demonic power
Only those sent by God can perform true miracles
Miracles are illusions created by human faith
Signs prove that the healer is a sinner
questions.correctAnswer: Only those sent by God can perform true miracles
questions.explanation: John 9:33 teaches that if a man were not from God, he could do nothing, affirming that true miracles are from divine authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 9:31 specifically demonstrate?
options: God's attentiveness to those who do His will
questions.correctAnswer: God's attentiveness to those who do His will
questions.explanation: John 9:31 declares that God hears not sinners but listens to those who worship Him and do His will, showing God's responsiveness and justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by Jesus' action in John 9:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over time and opportunity
questions.explanation: In John 9:4, Jesus speaks of working while it is day because the night comes when no one can work, demonstrating divine sovereignty over the timing of His mission.

questions.question: How does John 9:6-7 connect to the Old Testament theme of creation and divine power?
options: It shows Jesus as a new creator by forming clay and giving sight
It depicts a ritual unrelated to creation themes
It emphasizes human power over creation
It denies any creative act in healing
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Jesus as a new creator by forming clay and giving sight
questions.explanation: Jesus making clay with spittle and restoring sight recalls God's creative act of forming man from the dust (Genesis 2:7), connecting healing with divine creative power.

questions.question: In what way does John 9:39-41 fulfill a larger biblical theme about judgment and spiritual blindness?
options: It asserts that all physical blindness is punishment
It reveals Jesus’ mission to bring spiritual sight and to judge unbelief
It denies any judgment associated with spiritual insight
It limits judgment only to Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Jesus’ mission to bring spiritual sight and to judge unbelief
questions.explanation: John 9:39-41 shows Jesus explaining His mission to give sight to the blind and blind the seeing, applying judgment to spiritual blindness, aligning with prophetic themes of salvation and judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses John 9:24 and John 9:25 teach about the relationship between faith and knowledge of sin?
options: Faith requires full knowledge of sin
Faith can exist even without certainty about the sinfulness of the object of faith
Faith is impossible without doctrinal clarity
Faith is a human work to overcome sin
questions.correctAnswer: Faith can exist even without certainty about the sinfulness of the object of faith
questions.explanation: In John 9:24-25, the healed man does not know if Jesus is a sinner but believes in the healing, demonstrating faith apart from full understanding of sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses John 9:14 and John 9:16 teach about Jesus’ relationship to the Law and Sabbath?
options: Jesus violated the Sabbath without justification
Jesus’ works reveal divine authority that transcend Sabbath restrictions
Jesus’ healing was accidental on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ works reveal divine authority that transcend Sabbath restrictions
questions.explanation: John 9:14 and 9:16 show Jesus healing on the Sabbath, leading to Pharisaic debate, indicating Jesus’ authority to fulfill and transcend the Law.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses John 9:18 and John 9:22 teach about the social consequences of confessing Christ in the Jewish community of the time?
options: Confessing Christ risked expulsion from the synagogue
Confessing Christ was irrelevant to social standing
Parents were always supportive of confessing Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Confessing Christ risked expulsion from the synagogue
questions.explanation: John 9:18 and 9:22 reveal fear among the man’s parents because the Jews had agreed to expel anyone confessing Christ, showing the social and religious consequences of faith.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jesus’ healing of the blind man in John 9:13-34 was merely a natural recovery or deception. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The healing was a natural recovery explained by medical means
The blind man's testimony and the Pharisees' interrogation affirm a miraculous, divine healing
The healing was staged by Jesus’ disciples
The man never was blind and only pretended
questions.correctAnswer: The blind man's testimony and the Pharisees' interrogation affirm a miraculous, divine healing
questions.explanation: John 9:13-34 includes the man’s consistent testimony and the Pharisees' investigation, confirming the miracle was genuine and not natural or deceptive.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine revelation and human response is emphasized in John 9:37-38?
options: Sight of Jesus leads to worship and belief
questions.correctAnswer: Sight of Jesus leads to worship and belief
questions.explanation: In John 9:37-38, the healed man declares belief and worships Jesus after recognizing Him, teaching that divine revelation prompts true faith and worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly revealed in Jesus’ question in John 9:35 to the man cast out?
questions.correctAnswer: Compassion and personalized care
questions.explanation: Jesus seeking out the man in John 9:35 and personally asking if he believes shows God's compassionate and personal involvement in salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about sin and judgment is taught in John 9:1-2 and John 9:41?
options: Physical blindness is always punishment for sin
Spiritual blindness results in remaining sin and judgment
Sin has no relation to blindness
Only parents are held accountable for a child's sin
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual blindness results in remaining sin and judgment
questions.explanation: John 9:1-2 clarifies physical blindness is not due to sin, while John 9:41 states that claiming to see spiritually means sin remains, teaching about spiritual blindness and judgment.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from John 9:30 and John 9:32 about the recognition of Jesus’ divine origin?
options: Miracles prove nothing about Jesus’ origin
Jesus’ miraculous acts are unprecedented and evidence of divine origin
Jesus’ origin is irrelevant to His miracles
The Pharisees fully accepted Jesus’ divine origin
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ miraculous acts are unprecedented and evidence of divine origin
questions.explanation: John 9:30 and 9:32 emphasize the man’s amazement that Jesus opened his eyes, a miracle never heard of, affirming Jesus’ divine origin through His works.
